exposure: Fetal anomalies (e.g., congenital gastrointestinal anomalies, cleft palate, tracheoesophageal fistula, duodenal atresia)
outcome: Specific causes of polyhydramnios (idiopathic, gestational diabetes, fetal anomalies, multiple pregnancies, Rh isoimmunization)
Management strategies for polyhydramnios (reductive amniocentesis, indomethacin)
Mode of delivery (vaginal delivery, cesarean section)
Prevalence of polyhydramnios in primigravida patients
cohort: The study included 106 pregnant patients with clinically suspected polyhydramnios beyond 28 weeks of gestation who were managed at a tertiary care center.
finding: The primary finding was that nearly half of polyhydramnios cases were idiopathic (49.06%), with gestational diabetes (24.53%) and fetal anomalies (16.98%) being the next most significant contributors.
mod_finding: The majority of patients (79.2%) achieved vaginal delivery, while 20.8% underwent cesarean sections, indicating that most cases can be managed for a vaginal birth with proper care.
